Commentary.Commentary: We are back for Pakistan's second innings. South African players are out in the middle. Abid Ali and Imran Butt will open the innings for Pakistan. Kagiso Rabada will start the proceedings for South Africa.

Pakistan have a lead of 71 runs and would look to set a target of something upwards of 300 to put pressure on South Africa. Batting in the fourth innings will not be easy. On the other hand, South Africa would look to take quick wickets and put pressure on Pakistan. Join us in a while for Pakistan's second innings.

Coming to South Africa, they did not get off to a great start as they lost Elgar and Rassie van der Dussen early. Markram and du Plessis started to build a partnership but it was cut short by Faheem Ashraf who took the wicket of Faf du Plessis. Temba Bavuma was unbeaten on 44. He kept losing partners at the other end. South Africa skipper, Quinton de Kock also perished early on Day 3. Wiaan Mulder and George Linde supported Bavuma for a while but could not last long.
It has been a brilliant bowling performance from Pakistan. Hasan Ali ends the innings with a 5-fer. He was excellent with his line and lengths. Afridi and Ashraf took 1 wicket each.

OUT! TIMBER! That reverse swing coming back in has ensured that Nortje goes back for a duck. Hasan Ali also gets a 5-fer and he is absolutely ecstatic. He bowls a good length ball just outside the off pole, Nortje raises his blade and thinks about letting this one through to the keeper. He, though does not anticipate the ball to come back in. It tails in and goes onto clip the top of the off pole. Timber. SOUTH AFRICA END WITH 201! SOUTH AFRICA ALSO TRAIL BY 71 RUNS!

OUT! RUN OUT! Brilliant throw from Abid Ali! Very ordinary running from the South Africans and this is the second run out in the innings as well. On a good length and around off, Bavuma taps this one to the cover region and wants a quick single. Abid Ali is quick to run in and have a shy at the batter's end and he hits bullseye. Rabada was the man running in. The umpire thinks that this is out but wants the third umpire to confirm the same. Replays roll in and the third umpire completes the formality. South Africa are 9 wickets down now.

We are all set to begin Day 3. The Pakistan players are out in the middle. Temba Bavuma and Quinton de Kock will resume their innings for South Africa. Shaheen Afridi will start the proceedings for Pakistan for Day 3.

Hello and welcome to Day 3 of the 2nd Test between Pakistan and South Africa in Rawalpindi. The hosts would look to take quick wickets and put pressure on South Africa. Hasan Ali looked good yesterday as he took 2 wickets. On the other hand, South Africa would want Quinton de Kock and Temba Bavuma get going as their partnership would be crucial for the visitors. They trail by 166 runs and they would look to reduce the deficit as quickly as possible. Stay tuned for the updates.
... Day 3, Session 1 ...

A mixed day for both sides. Pakistan started poorly but finished well. They would have hoped to get somewhere close to 350 when Babar Azam and Fawd Alam were batting while the Proteas would have expected their batsmen to dig in a bit longer. There isn't much batting to come and the deficit is a big one. They might want to take a leaf out of Pakistan's book and bat sensibly, mixing caution with aggression. Onto Saturday then, the moving day. Day 3. How big a lead can Pakistan get? How closer to Pakistan's total can South Africa get? Join us at 9.45 am local (0445 GMT). Another early start and another long day. ADIOS! TAKE CARE!

A riveting final session. Pakistan managed to get 2 wickets, that of Aiden Markram and Faf du Plessis while the Proteas gathered 78 runs. 30 percent of those runs came in the last 10-15 minutes with de Kock coming out to bat in an aggressive manner. Pakistan could also have had Temba Bavuma, but he rode his luck, getting dropped, surviving an LBW call which was not chosen to be overturned by Pakistan and a couple of other close calls. He is hanging in there and will look to make his charmed life count, come Saturday.
The umpires get together for a chat. The light has deteriorated quite rapidly. Th floodlights are already on. Yup, that's it. The players walk off. STUMPS ON DAY 2, SOUTH AFRICA TRAIL BY 166!

DRINKS BREAK. Pakistan are making a very good fist of defending 272. They have already snared 3 wickets and have at least an hour to get though that middle order. Looking at the overs remaining (23), we might well be needing that extra half hour. This was supposed to be a trial by spin but it is the pacers who have done the damage. Markram will look to bat through the passage now.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Faheem gets the big wicket of Faf du Plessis. A pretty harmless delivery, on a length, outside off, Faf just looks to punch it through the line, without moving his feet. Gets a thick outside edge and Mohammad Rizwan does the rest. South Africa still trail by 217.
Good length ball on off, du Plessis blocks it off the front foot.

Another lovely drive. Full and outside off, Markram drives it down the ground, through the vacant mid off region. Babr Azam gives it a chase from cover, gets to the ball and flicks it back to the fielder running with him from mid on. Three runs taken. The stand moves to 22. 179 balls left in the day, 120 minutes remaining (extended).
Landed outside off, on a length, Faf shoulders arms.
Around middle, from around the wicket, pushed down to mid on.

FOUR! PRISTINE! What a delight to watch. Full and straight, around off, angling across, Faf just takes his left leg out of the way a bit, gets to the pitch of the ball and drives it straight back past the bowler, to his left, down the ground. Supreme insult to any fast bowler. The deficit is now 227.
Keeps the length a tad shorter than full, pushed towards cover again.

FOUR! Hasan gets a bit too greedy. He goes for the glory ball but bowls it too straight. Faf clips it through mid-wicket, with subtle use of his wrists. It is another no ball caught by the third umpire. 189 balls left in the day, 128 minutes remaining (extended).

That is a wide one, well outside off, fuller in length, left alone.
Full and around off, watchfully defended. No ball signalled by the third umpire for overstepping.

EDGED, FOUR! Not a bad ball at all, on the hat-trick chance. Hasan lands it on a length, around off, gets it to shape away, induces an outside edge as Faf du Plessis looks to defend but somehow, the ball goes to ground and threads a gap between slips and gully.
Time for the hat-trick ball. Hasan Ali took 2 wickets in 2 balls before Tea. Can he join the list?
Around middle, watchfully defended.
A short ball, pulled through square leg for a single to get off the mark.

This is pitched around middle, Markram comes forward and pushes it down the ground. By the time mid on can get across to his left, a single is pinched.

Welcome back for a slightly shortened session. Scheduled for 105 minutes. But we shall still have the 30-minute extension should the overs not be bowled. 33 left in the day. Here we go then, Shaheen Afridi to Aiden Markram. Faf du Plessis has joined him.
... DAY 2, SESSION 3 ...

What a stunning last over before Tea. Hasan Ali has found something which Shaheen Afridi could not. South Africa were rattling along but that last over before Tea has rattled them. That total of 272 now looks like something on the board. The visitors will be happy with the break as it has come at the right time. They would want to cool themselves and come back out with a positive mindset after Tea. 33 overs left in the day. Join us back in a while.

OUT! BOWLED! Two in two for Hasan Ali and he is pumped up! Pakistan are all over the moon. They were wayward in this 30-minute mini session but it has taken them two balls to be right on top. Full and straight, around off, van der Dussen looks to defend but the ball pitches, straightens and then shoots low. Beats the defensive prod and knocks the off stump out of the ground! Rassie walks back dejected and the umpires have a look at the clock. They feel there isn't time left for the new man to come. So TEA IT IS ON DAY 2, SOUTH AFRICA TRAIL BY 246!
Rassie van der Dussen walks out at number 3, with 3 minutes to Tea.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! The around-the-wicket angle works for Hasan. He was probing, probing, probing and eventually gets his reward. The line is full and outside off, shaping the ball away. The intention is to make Elgar reach out for the ball. From the straight angle, it seems like an unnecessary shot. But looking at it from Elgar's point of view, he has to play at it, because he is not sure whether the ball will come in or go away. No feet movement and the outside edge is taken this time. Easy catch for Mohammad Rizwan.
Outside off, on a length, Dean pushes but misses.

FOUR! EDGED AWAY! Two people look at the heavens with opposite reactions. The bowler looks in despair. Elgar looks in admonishment. Or perhaps thanks his stars. Full and outside off, Elgar pushes at it and gets a thick outside edge. But it goes between the slips and gully, to the third man fence.

The ball is shown to the umpires. They have a look and then hand it back to the players. Nothing is happening with the ball, no swing, no seam.
